text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To begin narrowing down the cause, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or speaking along with these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of worsening weakness with activity that improves with rest, combined with diplopia on vertical gaze, is highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of respiratory symptoms and family history helps rule out certain genetic or thymic causes, but the negative nerve stimulation test is atypical for Myasthenia Gravis. speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis (likely seronegative or with false-negative repetitive nerve stimulation).
